title: Projective logarithmic resolution over an excellent affine base
statement: Let $A$ be an excellent Noetherian ring [def-exc-excellent-ring], put $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $(V,M)$ be an integral fs log regular scheme, quasi-projective of finite type over $B$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective over a scheme $B$ means admitting a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$; projective means a closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$ followed by projection [def-kun-projective]. There exists a finite tower of saturated log blowups $b:(Y,M_Y)\to(V,M)$ whose underlying composite is projective and birational, with $Y$ integral and regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The log morphism $b$ is log etale [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. For any locally Noetherian fs log scheme $D$ and any log-smooth morphism $(V,M)\to D$, the composite $(Y,M_Y)\to D$ is log smooth. Birational means inducing an isomorphism between dense opens; length-zero towers are allowed.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.4.6(i), 3.4.8--Theorem 3.4.9, pp.111--112; VI 1.7--1.8, p.70; XVI 3.7, p.254. Finite normalized blowup towers are projective here; the quasi-projective affine-base hypothesis gives the finite-projective-space convention.

proof.text: Quasi-compactness of f over the affine base makes V quasi-compact (the quasi-compactness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]). At every geometric point apply [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart]. If g^n=1 for n>0, saturation puts both g and its inverse in the sharp characteristic monoid; their product is 1 by injectivity into the group completion, so sharpness gives g=1. Apply [lem-trf-monoidal-resolution-tower] to obtain one finite tower with free terminal characteristics.

Transport the initial equality of the chosen tower. The finite-tower assertion of [lem-sfb-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change] supplies its actual composites p and terminal log etaleness. Its IsIdentity condition gives equality of p_0 with the constructed identity: bases and every relative-test section map coincide. This yields the required HEq, including for length zero.

Log etale implies log smooth by [lem-sfb-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-log-smooth-preserves-log-regularity] to the terminal composite over the given log regular base. Its characteristic equivalences from the monoidal tower are converted from ULift of finitely supported natural tuples to finite natural tuples using the standard equivalences. The forward regularity conclusion of [lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary] gives IsRegularScheme of this terminal scheme.

For this same fixed tower use [lem-per-saturated-log-tower-projectivity], forgetting only the equation over the affine base in the quasi-projective witness. Use [lem-per-saturated-log-tower-dense-open] with the initial and terminal log regularity just established to obtain the dense-open isomorphism commuting with its composite.

The dense target open is nonempty and integral, as an open of the given integral base. Its isomorphic source open is irreducible. Closure preserves irreducibility and its density identifies that closure with the whole terminal scheme. Terminal regular local rings are domains by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], hence reduced; stalkwise reducedness gives reducedness of the scheme. A reduced irreducible nonempty scheme is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme].

Given any supplied log smooth map from V, apply the mixed-composition clause of [lem-sfb-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change] to its composite with the terminal log etale map. The CompEq equations determine all relative-test sections and identify the resulting log-smooth map with the explicit .comp in the conclusion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q160-7f62a01ce (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Fresh stage-1 split of the item re-admitted by the Q108 repair note: 11 steps and no new nodes. Compared with side-live, only the split fields changed; statement, source, stmt_deps, blueprint and the historical searches are preserved, and 8 new searches are appended. The item's closure has 10806 nodes and contains no id from the drop list. It does not use the excluded normalized-blowup route or any SGA source. Source check: ILO VIII 3.4.4, 3.4.6(i) and 3.4.8-3.4.9 (pp.110-112) and XVI 3.7 (pp.254-255: 'log-eclatement ... log-etale, projectif et birationnel, X''' regulier', log smooth over T) match the statement. Step checks: (1) P(n;B)=B x Proj Z[T] is identified with Proj A[T] through the scalar-extension node; shrinking to a quasi-compact open, the ample twist and restriction to the closed subscheme give an ample bundle on V. (2) A sharp saturated monoid has torsion-free group, so the monoidal-resolution hypotheses hold. (3) Z[P][L/z^e]=Z[Q_e] inside Z[P^gp] even when the group has torsion, so the fine blowup is a base change of a toric blowup and is proper over each chart. (4) Saturation is finite, which with fpqc descent gives properness of each stage; Noetherian and quasi-separated follow by induction. (5)-(6) Tautological polarization on each chart is canonical and generator-independent, so it glues; descent gives relative ampleness, then projective-bundle projectivity, composition over the qcqs base V, and H-projectivity from the ample bundle of step 1. (7) The formal-chart theorem applies with R=S=P, G=0, epsilon=1; h^{-1}(F)=0 because A->B is local; the completed forms come from the completed-chart node. (8) A characteristic monoid N^r gives a maximal ideal generated by r+d elements, hence regularity, descended from the strict henselization. (9) The trivial-characteristic locus is open and contains every generic point (rank 0 there), so it is dense. (10) That locus is preserved and reflected by each blowup, and the blowup is the identity over it, so b is birational; Y is irreducible and reduced, hence integral. (11) The log-calculus node gives that the tower is log etale and that the composite with a log-smooth map is log smooth. I tested length 0, P=0, a unit centre, r=d=0 and the A_1 singularity xy=z^2; no step fails. Duplicates: lem-trf-log-regular-desingularization is narrower (algebraically closed field, proper only); lem-per-gabber-log-blowup-regularization is on the drop list. Batch 5: none of the 16 flagged citations is a trace-formula or Poincare-duality step. The proof-only closures of sk-thm-trace-transport, cor-trf-point-counting and nt-target-poincare-isiso are disjoint from the item's closure. Every flagged node is a generic tool (Proj ampleness, log charts, monoidal resolution, log-blowup construction and descent, projectivity conventions, finitely generated groups, log calculus); the sfb nodes reach only trf definitions, and 5 generic pod module-foundation nodes are reached through the monoidal-resolution tower. All accepted. The 25 declared tool_uses are accepted as generic black boxes, since the Fourier unit gives none of them. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_projective_log_regular_resolution (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (hA : IsExcellent A) (V : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) [IsIntegral V.scheme] (hV : V.IsLogRegular) (f : V.scheme ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (hqp : ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : V.scheme ⟶ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1)); Spec (.of A))), IsImmersion i ∧ i ≫ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1)); Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A) = f) : ∃ (T : SaturatedLogBlowupTower.{u}) (p : ∀ i : Fin (T.length + 1), EtaleLogHom (T.level i) V), T.level 0 = V ∧ HEq (p 0) (EtaleLogHom.id V) ∧ (∀ i : Fin T.length, (T.arrow i).CompEq (p i.castSucc) (p i.succ)) ∧ IsHProjective (p (Fin.last T.length)).base ∧ (∃ (U : (T.level (Fin.last T.length)).scheme.Opens) (W : V.scheme.Opens) (e : U.toScheme ≅ W.toScheme), Dense (U : Set (T.level (Fin.last T.length)).scheme) ∧ Dense (W : Set V.scheme) ∧ U.ι ≫ (p (Fin.last T.length)).base = e.hom ≫ W.ι) ∧ IsIntegral (T.level (Fin.last T.length)).scheme ∧ IsRegularScheme (T.level (Fin.last T.length)).scheme ∧ (p (Fin.last T.length)).IsLogEtale ∧ ∀ (D : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (g : EtaleLogHom V D), g.IsLogSmooth → ((p (Fin.last T.length)).comp g).IsLogSmooth
